title: AL HJR51: Artificial Intelligence and Children's Internet Safety Study Commission, created

obligations: Study the effects of artificial intelligence, social media, and Internet access and usage on children (Sec. (c)(1)a)
Investigate how other states are working to provide innovative ways to protect children's health and safety in the face of widespread artificial intelligence and social media programs (Sec. (c)(1)b)
Develop recommendations for potential legislation to address these and related issues in this state (Sec. (c)(1)c)
As practicable, work with Alabama's Congressional delegation and the United States Department of Justice to coordinate efforts on these issues (Sec. (c)(2))
Hold the first meeting no later than May 1, 2026, and elect a chair and vice chair from among the membership (Sec. (d))
Prepare a report of findings, conclusions, and recommendations for proposed legislation to the Legislature no later than November 1, 2026 (Sec. (g))

Provide to the Secretary of State a notice of all meetings, the name of each member serving on the study commission, and a copy of the final report and other documents produced throughout the duration of the study commission (Sec. (h))

Appointing authorities shall coordinate their appointments to assure the study commission membership is inclusive and reflects the racial, gender, geographic, urban, rural, and economic diversity of the state (Sec. (b))

The Legislative Services Agency, the Clerk of the House of Representatives, and the Secretary of the Senate shall provide administrative and other assistance for the work of the study commission as necessary (Sec. (e))

body_html:
Passed 2026-03-10. Reading generated by ollama:deepseek-v4-pro from the enrolled text; the full text is at the foot of this page so every statement can be checked against it. LegiScan record · official text

What it does

Creates the Study Commission on Artificial Intelligence and Children's Internet Safety to study the effects of artificial intelligence, social media, and Internet access on children, investigate other states' approaches, and develop recommendations for potential legislation. The commission must report to the Legislature by November 1, 2026, and then dissolves.

Who it applies to

  • Members of the Study Commission on Artificial Intelligence and Children's Internet Safety, including two Senate members appointed by the President Pro Tempore, one Senate member appointed by the Minority Leader, two House members appointed by the Speaker, one House member appointed by the Minority Leader, the Attorney General or designee, one member appointed by the Commissioner of the Department of Mental Health, one member appointed by Voices for Alabama's Children, one member appointed by Alabama Cable and Broadband Association, one member appointed by TechNet, one member appointed by the Lieutenant Governor, and one member appointed by the Alabama Broadcasters Association
  • Appointing authorities named in the resolution
  • Legislative Services Agency, Clerk of the House of Representatives, and Secretary of the Senate for administrative assistance

Effective date

not stated in the text

Obligations

  • Study the effects of artificial intelligence, social media, and Internet access and usage on children (Sec. (c)(1)a)
  • Investigate how other states are working to provide innovative ways to protect children's health and safety in the face of widespread artificial intelligence and social media programs (Sec. (c)(1)b)
  • Develop recommendations for potential legislation to address these and related issues in this state (Sec. (c)(1)c)
  • As practicable, work with Alabama's Congressional delegation and the United States Department of Justice to coordinate efforts on these issues (Sec. (c)(2))
  • Hold the first meeting no later than May 1, 2026, and elect a chair and vice chair from among the membership (Sec. (d))
  • Prepare a report of findings, conclusions, and recommendations for proposed legislation to the Legislature no later than November 1, 2026 (Sec. (g))
  • Provide to the Secretary of State a notice of all meetings, the name of each member serving on the study commission, and a copy of the final report and other documents produced throughout the duration of the study commission (Sec. (h))
  • Appointing authorities shall coordinate their appointments to assure the study commission membership is inclusive and reflects the racial, gender, geographic, urban, rural, and economic diversity of the state (Sec. (b))
  • The Legislative Services Agency, the Clerk of the House of Representatives, and the Secretary of the Senate shall provide administrative and other assistance for the work of the study commission as necessary (Sec. (e))

Penalties and enforcement

not stated in the text

How it affects AI deployment

  • The resolution does not impose any direct requirements, prohibitions, or penalties on organisations that deploy AI; it only creates a study commission to examine effects and recommend future legislation (Sec. (c)(1), (g)).
  • Organisations deploying AI should monitor the commission's report due November 1, 2026, because it may contain recommendations for proposed legislation that could later affect AI deployment (Sec. (g)).

Compliance steps

  • If the organisation is an appointing authority named in the resolution, appoint one member to the study commission as specified (Sec. (a)(3) through (9)).
  • Coordinate appointments with other appointing authorities to assure the membership reflects the racial, gender, geographic, urban, rural, and economic diversity of the state (Sec. (b)).
  • If the organisation is a member of the study commission, attend the first meeting no later than May 1, 2026, and participate in electing a chair and vice chair (Sec. (d)).
  • Participate in the commission's duties: study effects, investigate other states, develop legislative recommendations, and coordinate with Congressional delegation and DOJ as practicable (Sec. (c)(1) and (c)(2)).
  • Contribute to the preparation of the report of findings, conclusions, and recommendations to the Legislature by November 1, 2026 (Sec. (g)).
  • Provide required information to the Secretary of State, including meeting notices, member names, and final report and documents (Sec. (h)).
  • For organisations not named as appointing authorities or members, no compliance steps are required by this resolution.
